construct: An accessory atrioventricular pathway directly connects atrial and ventricular myocardium, allowing part of the ventricle to depolarize before impulses traverse the AV node-His-Purkinje system. This produces a shortened PR interval and delta wave and can support macroreentrant atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A short PR interval, delta wave, and paroxysmal palpitations indicate ventricular pre-excitation through an accessory atrioventricular pathway that bypasses normal AV nodal delay.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Slow AV nodal conduction is tempting because it is a conduction disorder, but it lengthens rather than shortens the PR interval and cannot generate a delta wave.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Only accessory-pathway pre-excitation simultaneously explains the short PR, slurred QRS upstroke, and reentrant tachycardia substrate.
